title: Applied Digital's revenue soars, loss widens on growing AI investments
key_facts: Applied Digital's first-quarter revenue rose to $341.9 million from $80.9 million a year earlier, above analysts' average estimate of $133.8 million (LSEG data).
Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $221.0 million, or $0.76 a share, against $18.5 million, or $0.07 a share, a year earlier.
Total costs and expenses rose to $404.3 million from $90.7 million, due to higher spending to prepare data centres for customers, more stock-based pay and higher interest.
As of 31 August, Applied Digital had $3.7 billion in cash and restricted cash and $6.4 billion in debt.
Shares were up nearly 2% in volatile extended trading on Wednesday.
The Dallas, Texas company develops and operates data centres for AI and other high-performance computing.
quote_evidence: Applied Digital said costs rose due to higher spending to prepare data centers for customers, increased stock-based compensation and higher interest expenses as it expanded its AI infrastructure.

We are building for the long term, with a clear focus on developing large-scale, sustainable AI factory campuses and securing durable, high-quality, long-term contracts with proven, tier-one, investment-grade hyperscalers that are leaders in the AI industry, CEO Wes Cummins said in a statement.
why_it_matters_hint: The company is borrowing heavily to build AI data centres; one quarter's results show the cost of that growth.
